::: {.why}
A pricer you wrote and only checked against itself is a pricer with an undiscovered sign error, and the libraries exist precisely so you do not have to trust your own algebra.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement a Black-Scholes pricer with dividends and rates handled explicitly, and agree with py_vollib and QuantLib to a stated tolerance.
- Implement implied volatility by root-finding and state where it fails.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Write qlib/derivatives/black_scholes.py with the call and put prices, handling a continuous dividend yield and a rate explicitly rather than defaulting them to zero. Test against py_vollib across a grid of strikes, maturities and volatilities, and assert agreement to a tolerance you state.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Implement implied volatility by Newton's method with a bisection fallback, and find where it fails: deep out-of-the-money options where vega is nearly zero, and prices that violate the no-arbitrage bounds. Handle both explicitly rather than returning a wrong number.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/derivatives/black_scholes.py is the pricing layer for the rest of the phase, tested against an independent implementation and with implied volatility inversion that fails loudly rather than silently.
:::
